lines.text: The Strait of Hormuz shuts for a week. Which country runs out first?
Every day, about 20.9M barrels of oil sail through this one gap, a lane of sea between Iran's mountains and the tip of Oman.
Day one: the tankers stop. Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain are stuck behind the gate, and their ships have nowhere else to go.
Look at the map: every bit of their coast lies inside the Gulf, like a room with only one door.
Day two: Saudi Arabia has a way round, a pipeline west across the desert to the Red Sea.
Day three: the Emirates pipe oil to Fujairah, a port just outside the strait.
But those two pipes carry only a small part of what the tankers did, and the rest has nowhere to go.
Day four: no new tankers leave for China, India, Japan or South Korea, and most of the oil through Hormuz sails east to Asia.
And the strangest part? Iran ships most of its own oil from inside the Gulf too, from an island called Kharg.
So who runs out first? Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain run out of ways to sell their oil: this gap is their only road out, and it carries about 20% of all the oil the world uses.
Hormuz or Malacca: which strait should we shut next? Tell me below, while the Strait of Hormuz shuts for a week.
